text.p: The chairman of French first division club Nantes, Guy Scherrer, resigned on Wednesday.
"I quit FCNA (Football Club Nantes Atlantique)," Scherrer said in a brief statement. "As I took this decision for personal reasons, I will not make further comments."
Some members of the club's board have openly complained recently about Scherrer's methods, accusing him of never consulting them on important issues.

Businessman Scherrer became Nantes president in 1992 when the club, traditionally one of the best in French soccer, was struggling with heavy debts and threatened by relegation to the second division.
Scherrer improved the club's finances while the club pushed forward a bunch of talented players such as Christian Karembeu, Patrice Loko and Reynald Pedros.
The club took the French title in 1995 and went on to reach the semifinals of the Champions' League.

After selling several key players, they made a disastrous start to the current season but recovered in their recent outings and are now 16th in the 20-strong league, 14 points behind leaders Paris St Germain.
